text: Craters dominate the lunar landscape, appearing as massive geological scars visible in the thousands across the surface. These features result from ancient volcanic activity that also produced the great impact basins. The Aitken basin stands as the most extensive example, spanning nearly one-third of the moon and dating to an impact event roughly 3.9 billion years ago. An orbit describes the trajectory of a body circling another in space, whether that body is a planet or a satellite. In this system, the moon circles the Earth, while the Earth itself circles the sun.
